title: Your Submission Is Dangerous
author: Pondering Moore
summary: Pondering Moore uses the example of a Norse Pagan acquaintance's failed family dynamic to explore the Christian understanding of submission and its dangerous misapplication. Submission commanded without the corresponding love, sacrifice, and transformation of the one leading produces only resentment and strife. True family authority in the Christian frame requires the leader to undergo genuine moral transformation first—when that happens, submission follows naturally rather than through coercion.
points: All people submit to something; the question is not whether to submit but to what—the Norse pagan transactional relationship with gods mirrors many distorted views of family authority.
A man demanding submission from family members through provision alone—without accompanying love and self-transformation—produces resentment and strife rather than genuine relationship.
The Norse pagan ethos of bending no knee to the gods while submitting implicitly to community survival needs shows that all human systems require some form of structured deference.
When the father follows the example of Jesus Christ, the changes that result cannot be explained without grace—and they create the conditions for genuine, non-coerced family unity.
The Christian framework places the burden of transformation on the leader first: authority is not earned by provision alone but by demonstrated love and moral character.
